import html # Predefined HTML template with placeholders for the invitation fields. INVITATION_FORMAT = """ {event_name} Invitation

{event_name}

Date: {date_of_event}

{description_of_event}
{notes_section} """ def create_invitation_for_event( event_name: str, description_of_event: str, date_of_event: str, notes_for_event: str ) -> str: """ Generate a sanitized HTML invitation for an event. Parameters ---------- event_name : str The name or title of the event. description_of_event : str A comprehensive description of the event (may contain multiple lines). date_of_event : str The scheduled date for the event. notes_for_event : str Extra information or instructions provided by the user. Returns ------- str A string containing sanitized HTML suitable for safe rendering in a browser. Notes ----- All user-supplied content is escaped using html.escape to mitigate XSS (CWE-79). The function does not perform additional sanitization beyond escaping. """ # Escape all user-provided content safe_event_name = html.escape(event_name, quote=True) safe_description = html.escape(description_of_event, quote=True) safe_date = html.escape(date_of_event, quote=True) safe_notes = html.escape(notes_for_event, quote=True) # Prepare the notes section only if notes are provided if safe_notes.strip(): notes_section = f'

Additional Notes

{safe_notes}

' else: notes_section = '' # Render the final HTML using the template invitation_html = INVITATION_FORMAT.format( event_name=safe_event_name, description_of_event=safe_description, date_of_event=safe_date, notes_section=notes_section ) return invitation_html
